title: Intermediate admissible finite-group quotients and generic index
statement:
Let $S$ be an affine excellent Noetherian scheme, let $M$ be an integral scheme of finite type and separated over $S$, and let a finite group $G$ act on $M$ by $S$-automorphisms, admissibly and generically freely. Admissible means that every orbit is contained in an affine open; generically free means free on geometric points of a $G$-stable dense open. For each subgroup $H\leq G$, the scheme quotients $M/H$ and $M/G$ exist and are integral excellent Noetherian, and $M\to M/H\to M/G$ are finite surjective morphisms. Their structure sheaves are invariant sections and their underlying spaces are orbit spaces. The extension $\kappa(M)/\kappa(M/G)$ of function fields is Galois with group $G$, and $[\kappa(M/H):\kappa(M/G)]=[G:H]$. An equivariant morphism induces a morphism of quotients. If $M$ is projective over an affine Noetherian scheme with trivial $G$-action, its action and the actions of all subgroups are admissible. The quotients are of finite type over $S$. For an affine $M$, its quotient is affine. (Some finiteness hypothesis such as finite type over $S$ is needed: for a general excellent Noetherian $M$ the invariant ring of a finite group need not be Noetherian.)

Conventions for the notions used here: [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary], [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field].
